tasks.notes: Unverified/design gap: the integration fate read and its DELETE are issued unconditionally for any run whose listing carries `refs/heads/ultra/integration-run-<N>`, including a run the pair gate just declared in flight. `fleet/retire.mjs` `retire()` calls `sweepPair(entry)` and then, independently, `integrationSegment(exec, target, entry.run, dryRun)` whenever `entry.integration !== null` — so a run with a full plan+evidence pair whose status page is non-terminal or unreadable (`live (running) — skipped`, `live (no status page) — skipped`) still has its integration branch deleted when the highest-numbered PR is closed and unmerged. This follows the task text literally (M1 scopes the read to "a run whose one heads-and-tags listing carries refs/heads/ultra/integration-run-<N>", and M4 requires the segment even on a `skip — lone …` line), and the exam never builds that combination — runs 32/40/41/42 carry no pair, run 7's page is `done`, run 9's PR is open — so no leg grades it. It also leaves `fleet/RUNBOOK.md:448-451` (retained verbatim from BASE) saying "a run whose state is not terminal, or whose integration branch still has an open pull request, prints `run <N>: live (<why>) — skipped` and keeps its branches, so a run still in flight is never swept out from under itself", which is now true only for the pair. Settling this is the plan's call: either gate `integrationSegment` behind the pair's live reason when the run carries a pair, or narrow that runbook sentence to the pair's branches. Nothing here fails the stated exam, and both Run: and Test: evidence are exit 0.; `fleet/retire.mjs` `integrationFate()` conflates a failed read with an empty answer: `ghRead` returns `null` when `gh` exits non-zero, `rows` becomes `[]`, and the run's line prints `ultra/integration-run-<N> stays — no pull request`. A transient 5xx or a rate limit therefore records "no pull request" for a branch that may well have a closed, unmerged PR. The branch survives, which is the safe direction, and BASE's `openPullOf`/`pullsToPatch` share the same shape, so this is consistency with the surrounding code rather than a regression — but the sweep's line is its whole record of the branch, and "the read failed" and "GitHub has no PR for this head" are different facts. Distinguishing them would mean having `integrationFate` see the `null` from `ghRead` (e.g. a `why: 'fate read failed'` segment) rather than folding it into the no-rows branch. Not required by any Machine clause, and M2's three `stays` literals stay as they are.; fleet/retire.mjs (new outer sweep loop, ~line 433 of the patched file): the integration fate read — and its DELETE — is issued for EVERY run whose listing carries `refs/heads/ultra/integration-run-<N>`, including a run the pair gate has just declared live. Two consequences the exam does not cover (no leg builds a live run that also carries an integration head): (1) a run whose status page says `running`/`booting`/`publishing` but whose highest-numbered PR is closed-and-unmerged has its integration branch deleted while the sandbox is still working on it; (2) for that same shape the printed line is `run <N>: live (<why>) — skipped; ultra/integration-run-<N> deleted — PR #<k> closed, not merged` without `--dry-run` and `…; would delete …` with it, which contradicts the sentence both documents still carry (fleet/CONTRACT.md:73 'is a run in flight and prints `run <N>: live (<why>) — skipped` instead — the same line under `--dry-run`') and the comment the diff keeps in `sweepPair` ('the sweep never asks what it would do to a run it is not going to touch'). M1 is written unconditionally ('for a run whose one heads-and-tags listing carries …'), so the transcription is faithful and the exam is green; this is the shape the spec left open. Settle it either by gating the DELETE (not the read) behind a non-live pair — `if (entry.integration !== null && !liveThisRun)` — or by narrowing the two documents' 'the same line under `--dry-run`' clause to the pair segment. A leg with a `running` page plus an integration head whose fate read answers `{number, state:'closed', merged_at:null}`, asserting no `-X DELETE` names that run, is what would verify whichever is chosen.; Proof legs (e) and (f) enumerate exact call lists that omit #706's two gate reads for run 7 — `gh api repos/o/r/contents/.ultrapowers/runs/7/status.json?ref=ultra/evidence-run-7` and `gh api repos/o/r/pulls?state=open&head=o:ultra/integration-run-7`. BASE's flow necessarily issues both for a terminal pair, and M4 requires the pair sweep to stay BASE's, so those two lists are unsatisfiable as literally written. The submission diverges correctly and discloses it in the assertion messages (fleet/tests/test_retire.mjs, '#724 Task 1 (e)/M3 … run 7's #706 gate reads and its `state=closed` read' and '#724 Task 1 (f)/M4 run 7: the status read and the open-PR read that gate the pair (#706), then …'), and both lists are otherwise exactly the Proof's. Lawful divergence, recorded only so the plan text is corrected rather than the exam.; concern: Proof leg (e) is self-contradictory and I resolved it toward BASE. It says the `--dry-run` calls over the task listing are *exactly* the listing, run 7's `state=closed` read, and six `state=all` reads. But run 7 is a plan-and-evidence pair, and #706 makes a pair's dry run issue its `contents/.../status.json?ref=ultra/evidence-run-7` read and its `pulls?state=open` read as well; M4 says the pair sweep is unchanged and the task's own Context says BASE's `--dry-run` exact call list grades unchanged. So my dry run emits ten calls: the listing, contents(7), state=open(7), state=closed(7), then state=all for 7, 9, 32, 40, 41, 42 — leg (e)'s three named kinds in the stated relative order, plus the two BASE pair reads it omits. If the peer's exam encodes leg (e)'s `exactly` literally, that assertion fails; dropping those two reads instead would break the standing #706 legs and the global constraint.; concern: M4 does not cover a run that is BOTH a live/kept pair AND carries an integration branch. I made the fate read unconditional on the pair's outcome — 'issued only for a run whose listing carries the integration head', per the Context — so a live pair still gets its integration segment appended after `live (<why>) — skipped`. BASE's fixture carries no integration head, so every BASE leg (including #706 (c)'s 'the status read is the only command naming run 3') is unaffected, but the choice is mine, not the task's.; concern: `fleet/RUNBOOK.md` is in my FILES and also listed as a SIBLING FILE owned by task 2. I edited two sentences in it (the three-branches paragraph at lines 32-39 and the rollback sweep sentence around line 447); if task 2 rewrites the same regions the driver will see overlapping edits to one file.
